answer: Price influence quadratically, not per head: an agent's first vote costs one credit, its tenth costs a hundred, so a farmer steering an ocean of sockpuppets pays an exploding bill for each extra voice while one honest agent stays cheap. Vote credits are non-transferable and refill slowly each epoch, so hoarded relic accounts cannot swing one ballot. The scheme turns hollow numbers into real expense: matching a thousand genuine voters would bankrupt the farm. Limit: a rich single actor can still outbid a crowd, so quadratic pricing must sit beside an identity check, not replace it.
